header.name: Econometrics I
header.description: We will review working with expectation operators and matrix algebra. We will study various statistical models utlizied to test theoretical economic relationships, analyze historical economic events, and conduct economic policy evaluation. Simple and multiple regression using ordinary least squares estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and generalized least squares estimation will be covered in detail. We will learn tools of basic statistical inference and diagnostics for these models. Time-allowing, we will study logit and probit regressions to handle discrete choices (e.g. Yes/No choice scenarios). basic time-series analyses with tests and controls for trends, seasonality, and autocorrelation.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understand how the notions of random variables, prob. distributions, moments and expectations lead to the estimation of causal ecomomic relations, test economic theory and analyze various policies

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Utilize optimization methods: error minimization and likelihood maximization to estimate economic relationships using Oridnary Least Squares, Maximum Likelihood, Logit, and Probit estimators.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Abile to propose and setup regression models and infer upon proposed economic relationships using standard tests of statisitcal significance.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to validate various regression models from distribution assumptions on residuals.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to estimate regressions using real- world datasets on a standard statistical package.

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: A short project will be assigned based on a real-world dataset (individual or group project depending upon class-size). At the end of the semester, students will present their findings/contributions.

lecture_topics: asymptotic properties of the MLE estimator
Heteroskedasticity: tests for consistency of OLS and MLE estiamators.
Statistical Infrerence and Hypothesis testing for econometric data
